items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: I remember Fats was my first idol, and then Hines and then Art.

ctx.x: But eventually, it will come out -- the writing will come out pure, clear, loud and clean. If you just keep trying and don't back away from it, as over a period of time they will, so I think a young player, when they are developing an improvising style of your own. Because ideas do come to you, and of course the safe thing is -- we all start out idolizing someone. I remember Fats was my first idol, and then Hines and then Art.

And to break away from that, at a certain point, you must break away from that and let your own musical sense tell you what to try for, instead of the stuff you learned from your idols. That takes a little courage -- because you know when you've been copying a successful guy, and you know that's good. What you learn from, and you don't know whether your own stuff, whether you should go back to playing like so and so, when you start on your own.
